name: Shopify
tagline: Shopify's subscription UX is a behavioral design case study in how defaults, anchoring, and progressive commitment turn free trials into long-term subscriptions.
key_insight: Shopify shows how behavioral design can serve both platform and user goals simultaneously. The setup wizard uses progressive commitment, but the merchant genuinely gets a working store. The $1 trial uses anchoring, but the merchant genuinely gets to test the platform risk-free. The app ecosystem creates lock-in, but it also creates genuine value. This alignment between behavioral technique and user outcome is what separates ethical persuasion from manipulation.
top_evidence: Merchant retention 68% → 82% after $1/3mo trial (est. from Q4 2024 earnings). Merchants completing 5+ setup steps have 3.2x higher 90-day retention.

techniques.title: Trial-to-Paid Default Architecture
techniques.description: Shopify's $1/month for 3 months offer reframes the purchase decision from 'pay $39/mo or leave' to 'pay $1 or lose everything you built.' The $1 price exploits two biases simultaneously: anchoring ($1 vs $39 makes $39 seem reasonable later) and sunk cost (you've already built your store). The transition from $1 to full price happens automatically — the default is to continue.
techniques.evidence: Shopify's merchant retention rate increased from 68% to 82% after introducing the $1/3mo trial (estimated from Shopify Q4 2024 earnings). The default auto-renewal pattern matches Thaler & Sunstein's findings on opt-out organ donation.

techniques.title: Setup Wizard as Progressive Commitment
techniques.description: Shopify's onboarding breaks store creation into 7-8 discrete steps (add product → choose theme → set shipping → configure payments). Each step creates a micro-investment and reveals the next step — classic progressive disclosure. By the time a merchant has completed setup, they've invested 2-4 hours and feel committed even before making a single sale.
techniques.evidence: Shopify's 2023 UX research: merchants who complete 5+ setup steps have 3.2x higher 90-day retention than those who complete <3 steps. The commitment escalation mirrors Cialdini's consistency principle.

techniques.title: App Store as Ecosystem Lock-In
techniques.description: The Shopify App Store (8,000+ apps) creates an Investment loop that makes switching extremely costly. Each app a merchant installs (email marketing, reviews, SEO tools) deepens their commitment. The Investment phase of the Hook Model is traditionally the weakest — Shopify makes it the strongest by externalizing it to a marketplace ecosystem.
techniques.evidence: Average Shopify merchant uses 6 third-party apps (Shopify Partner Report, 2024). Switching cost = reconfiguring 6 integrations on a new platform. This ecosystem moat is the primary reason Shopify's merchant retention exceeds WooCommerce and BigCommerce.

strengths: Setup wizard is textbook progressive commitment
App ecosystem creates value alongside switching costs
weaknesses: Auto-renewal from $1 to full price catches some off-guard
Plan comparison uses anchoring that may not reflect needs
